draft.title: Enzymes
card: Enzymes are proteins that act as catalysts in living things. They speed up a reaction by giving it a lower activation energy, and they are not used up.
Each enzyme has an active site, a small region with a specific shape. Only a substrate that fits the site can bind, and the reaction happens there.

Protein structure has levels. Primary is the sequence of amino acids. Secondary is folding into helices and sheets. Tertiary is the 3D shape of the whole chain. Quaternary is several chains joined together.
Heat or a change in pH can break the bonds that hold the tertiary shape. The active site changes shape, the substrate no longer fits, and the enzyme is denatured.
draft.remember: An enzyme works only while its active site keeps its shape. Heat and pH change can ruin that shape.

a.q: Why does a very high temperature stop an enzyme from working?
opts: The active site changes shape, so the substrate cannot fit
The amino acid sequence is rearranged into a new order
The enzyme is used up by the reaction it catalyses
The substrate is changed so it can no longer react
a.why: High temperature breaks the bonds that hold the tertiary shape, so the active site no longer matches the substrate. The primary structure is the amino acid sequence, and it is not rearranged by this change.
a.clue: Think about what holds the 3D shape in place.

b.q: A digestive enzyme in Priya's stomach works well at very low pH. She tests it in a solution at neutral pH and it stops working. What is the best explanation?
opts: The change in pH altered the shape of its active site
The enzyme was used up as it catalysed the reaction
The change in pH rearranged its amino acid sequence
The change in pH made the substrate unable to react
b.why: A change in pH can break the bonds that hold the tertiary shape, so the active site no longer fits the substrate. The primary structure is the amino acid sequence, and it is not rearranged by this change.
b.clue: Which level of structure sets the shape of the active site?

a.best: The active site changes shape, so the substrate cannot fit

b.best: The change in pH altered the shape of its active site
